### POP.gvn_legitimacy
- P001a (memo 001) pushes +2 [old band ≈ +5..+7] — The government's return to a hamlet no longer means the landlord's return; for the first time it gives the peasant something the Viet Cong cannot take away by winning
- P001b (memo 001) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — Visible prosecution of officials who prey on the population, if it reaches above the district level
- P002a (memo 002) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — A policeman who settles disputes, records crime and arrests on evidence is the government's most frequent face in the village; the gain reverses where the police extort or torture
- P002b (memo 002) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — The district chief is the government in the countryside; one who is resident, competent and not for sale changes what the government means in his district
- P011c (memo 011) pushes +0..+1 (low) on POP.gvn_legitimacy.I_corps — One village in Quang Ngai not emptied by its allies; a trace in a province the Front had held for a generation

### POP.night_control
- P001a (memo 001) depends — A title delivered by day to a hamlet the VC hold by night is a death warrant; delivery follows security
- P002a (memo 002) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — A police post that sleeps in the village adds a resident presence and a radio; it holds only where Popular Forces stand with it and a reaction arrives in the dark (POSTNA-2)
- P002b (memo 002) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — A district chief who knows his villages and keeps his Popular Forces in them at night, rather than in the district town, is the mechanism of night control
- P002a (memo 002) depends — A resident constable in a village held by the VC at night is a target, not a policeman; posts follow security
- P002b (memo 002) depends — A competent chief in a district the enemy holds by night is a competent chief in a besieged town
- P004a (memo 004) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — Hamlet outposts that hold a night longer because their garrisons are not outgunned; small, real, and dependent on whether the platoon is awake and present
- P006a (memo 006) depends — An arrest in a village the enemy holds at night is a raid, and its informant is dead the next week
- P008b (memo 008) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — Hamlets and outposts that can summon fire and reaction forces after dark are harder to overrun or intimidate
- P008a (memo 008) depends — Power lines from Da Nhim, rail and roads to the plants run through contested country
- P008b (memo 008) depends — A radio in a hamlet the Front holds at night is the Front's radio
- P009c (memo 009) depends — A trained PF platoon matters only in a hamlet it is posted to and stays in after dark
- P010b (memo 010) depends — The schooled PF platoon leader matters only in a hamlet his platoon holds after dark and a reaction force that comes when he calls

### STRIKE.responsiveness
- P003b (memo 003) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — A live track passed to a strike controller by line-of-sight or satellite link (E01) cuts the time from detection to ordnance where an aircraft is already airborne; it does nothing where the strike asset is an hour away
- P003a (memo 003) depends — A location from the U-2 is worth what can be done with it in the hours it stays true
- P003b (memo 003) depends — A track is worth a strike aircraft within twenty to forty minutes of it; the historical force must be airborne or on strip alert to use it
- P005a (memo 005) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — Unrefuelled reach from Guam and fewer tankers shorten the planning chain; still hours, not minutes
- P005c (memo 005) depends — The bomb is fast; the B-52 mission planning chain is not
- P006c (memo 006) depends — Much of the adviser's standing comes from the American fire and lift he can call
- P008b (memo 008) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — More territorial and ARVN stations on the fire-support nets, kept working by local repair
- P008b (memo 008) depends — A call for help is worth what the artillery and reaction force behind it can do
- P010b (memo 010) depends — The American course teaches the squad leader to fix and call fire; his competence depends on fire the RVNAF does not own (F010-24)

### SUBVERT.defection
- P001a (memo 001) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — Southern-born guerrillas and their families can now keep land the Front gave them without the Front; slow and confined to areas the government can reach
- P002a (memo 002) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — A resident constable and a Special Branch officer are a door a frightened cadre can walk through at night; Special Branch, not the Army, debriefs and turns ralliers
- P004a (memo 004) depends — Weapons-for-money and Chieu Hoi rewards meet a market in which a modern carbine is the most valuable thing a man can carry
- P006a (memo 006) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — Targeted offers to named cadres and exploitation of each rallier's knowledge
- P006a (memo 006) depends — Ralliers are the richest source of the network map

### US.credibility_gap
- P001b (memo 001) pushes -1 [old band ≈ -4..-2] — Independent musters and audits give MACV strength and expenditure figures that do not pass through the reporting chain (G-10)
- P002b (memo 002) pushes -1 [old band ≈ -4..-2] — An Inspectorate that verifies province reporting gives MACV a check on figures produced by the men rated on them (A13)
- P006a (memo 006) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — An American-designed targeting programme is a press story from 1965, whatever its rules
- P006c (memo 006) pushes -1 [old band ≈ -4..-2] — Advisers with protected careers and language report what they see
- P011c (memo 011) pushes -3..-1 (medium) — No cover-up to come apart in November 1969: the starkest single proof that MACV's reports could hide a massacre never reaches the press

### US.political_tolerance
- P001b (memo 001) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — Visible reform and true strength returns modestly lengthen tolerance, with negative spikes from corruption headlines (F001-14)
- P001a (memo 001) depends — Congress funds the compensation bonds over eight years
- P001b (memo 001) depends — Washington must accept slower military operations while commands are purged
- P002a (memo 002) depends — Congress funds a police programme that its critics will call a secret police
- P002b (memo 002) depends — Washington must accept that a chief who will not falsify returns reports bad news
- P003a (memo 003) depends — A lost U-2 is a public event; the 1960 and 1962 losses are in every politician's memory
- P004a (memo 004) pushes +1 [old band ≈ +2..+4] — Small: no 1967 rifle scandal, no Ichord subcommittee hearings, no letters home about a rifle that jams; fewer dead in the first seconds of contact
- P005a (memo 005) depends — Every expansion of B-52 targeting is a Washington decision
- P006a (memo 006) depends — A programme described as assassination can be ended by Congress
- P006b (memo 006) depends — No reserve mobilization; the rotation base comes from the active forces and the draft
- P007a (memo 007) depends — The training base and the officers' time in school are paid for in a war Congress funds by year
- P007c (memo 007) depends — The aid condition behind the board is only as strong as Washington's willingness to suspend aid to an ally at war over a general
- P008a (memo 008) depends — The aid appropriation pays for propellant, explosive, electrodes and alloys; the arsenal's value after 1973 is set by what Congress votes
- P008b (memo 008) depends — Semiconductors, crystals and licences after 1973 are bought with appropriated dollars
- P009a (memo 009) depends — Two more weeks in the pipeline for every soldier during the 1965–66 build-up
- P010a (memo 010) depends — Men in school and gated promotions during a build-up without reserve mobilisation
- P011a (memo 011) pushes +4..+7 (medium) on US.political_tolerance.administration — From mid-1973 the President keeps his authority, his staff and his attention; the man who wrote Thieu his assurances is still in office to keep them, as far as Congress lets him
- P011a (memo 011) pushes +2..+4 (low) on US.political_tolerance.congress — A smaller 1974 midterm swing and no Republican collapse in 1973–74; Case–Church probably still passes, the War Powers override and the depth of the 1974–75 aid cuts are what is at stake
- P011a (memo 011) pushes +0..+1 (medium) on US.political_tolerance.public — The 'mistake' share stood at about 60% in 1971 and in 1973 before Watergate peaked; the scandal moved trust in the President, not opinion of the war
- P011b (memo 011) pushes +1..+3 (medium) on US.political_tolerance.public — A quarter fewer induction notices in every town every month; fewer families whose son was taken against his will, fewer draftee dead; the draft was the war's sharpest domestic grievance
- P011b (memo 011) pushes +0..+2 (low) on US.political_tolerance.congress — Smaller draft calls take some heat out of the extension fights of 1967 and 1971 and of the constituency mail; Congress votes on the war for reasons the draft only sharpens
- P011c (memo 011) pushes +0..+2 (low) on US.political_tolerance.public — Mass opinion sided with Calley in 1971; the damage My Lai did was to elite, press and congressional opinion and to the moral case against the war, which loses its emblem
- P011a (memo 011) depends — Everything it buys is a change in what Washington will grant in 1973–75

- P002a (memo 002) pushes -1 [old band ≈ -4..-2] — The family census shows which sons have gone to the forest and makes VC conscription in held villages visible and costly; confined to held villages, and partly offset by youths who leave before the census reaches them

- P006a (memo 006) pushes -1 [old band ≈ -4..-2] — Cadres above the hamlet named, arrested and tried from 1965 rather than 1968, where night security exists

- P001a (memo 001) pushes -1 [old band ≈ -4..-2] — Owner-cultivators with a title to defend are harder to tax by consent; coercive taxation in VC-held hamlets is untouched
- P002a (memo 002) pushes -1 [old band ≈ -4..-2] — Resource control on roads and waterways and a constable in the market town raise the cost of moving tax rice and cash

## Settled positions on these variables

- **POSTNA-1** · vars: GVN.political_stability, POP.gvn_legitimacy, POP.land_tenure · The binding deficit on the opening date is political: no provision that leaves the Saigon government's standing in the countryside unchanged moves the end state above rung (b), whatever it does to the enemy's forces (TNA G-1)
- **POSTNA-2** · vars: POP.night_control, RFPF.effectiveness · Night control of a hamlet is held only by security resident in it with a means of calling help and a reaction that arrives in the dark; mobile forces that leave at dusk do not change it (TNA G-2)
- **POSTNA-3** · vars: ENEMY.engagement_control, ENEMY.regeneration, SANCT.laos, SANCT.cambodia · While the enemy controls whether to accept battle and regenerates in sanctuary, attrition has no crossover point; a strategy that waits for one waits for something the geometry does not permit (TNA G-8)
- **POSTNA-5** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.credibility_gap, US.casualties · The American political clock is spent by casualties, cost and time, and fastest by the discovery that reported progress was false; a provision that improves a metric without improving the war shortens the clock (TNA G-5, G-10)
- **POSTNA-6** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, POP.gvn_legitimacy · Advisory leverage trades short-run effectiveness against long-run legitimacy; no position on that line is free, and every proposal to increase leverage states what it costs the Republic's claim to be its own government (TNA G-6)
- **POS001-1** · vars: POP.land_tenure, POP.gvn_legitimacy, POP.night_control · Land reform changes what the government's arrival means, not whether it arrives: its value in any hamlet equals the night security behind it, and titles issued are never evidence of allegiance (001 §2 F001-4, F001-10; §4.P2)
- **POS001-2** · vars: GVN.corruption, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · An independent anti-corruption body in the Republic survives only with a Vietnamese patron and an American lever; its durable effect is on muster, pay and documentary cases below the top, and its reach upward ends when the lever lapses with the American drawdown (001 §4.P4)
- **POS001-4** · vars: POP.gvn_legitimacy, VCI.strength · A one-band gain in the countryside's allegiance does not carry into the conventional battles of 1972 and 1975; the end state turns on the military balance after the American withdrawal, and political gains are necessary but not sufficient to move it (001 §4.N)
- **POS002-1** · vars: GVN.police, FIND.vci, POP.night_control · A rural police and Special Branch attack the infrastructure, not the main force; their value in any village equals the night security beside them, and where they work best their arrest count falls, so arrest counts and quotas are never the measure of them (002 F002-11, F002-17; §4.P2)
- **POS002-2** · vars: GVN.admin_capacity, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · Merit selection of province and district chiefs survives the coups only with the American aid lever behind it; when the lever lapses with the drawdown the President captures the Board without abolishing it, and its durable gain is the chiefs' experience below the palace (002 §4.P4, EV002-6)
- **POS002-3** · vars: GVN.police, GVN.political_stability, POP.gvn_legitimacy · A stronger and better-recorded police in a coup-prone state is used by the government of the day against its domestic opposition, and its records are a list of loyalties the enemy can capture; both costs are paid and do not outweigh the gain in the held belt (002 F002-9, F002-16; §4.P2, §4.P3)
- **POS003-1** · vars: FIND.main_force, FIX.capability, STRIKE.responsiveness · Airborne radar and signals reconnaissance find the enemy's movement in the open and his headquarters' transmitters, never his regiments under canopy; their value in any engagement equals what can be put on a track within the hour, and an improvement in finding is never claimed as an improvement in fixing (003 §2 F003-5; §4.P2–P5)
- **POS003-3** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.credibility_gap · In this war no attack of 4 August 1964 was claimed and Pierce Arrow was not flown; the Southeast Asia Resolution rests on the attack of 2 August, and the Tonkin deception is not part of the credibility gap in any later phase (003 §4.P1, §4.P3; EV000-3)
- **POS004-1** · vars: RFPF.effectiveness, POP.night_control, ENEMY.engagement_control · Infantry small arms change how the fights the enemy accepts go, never which fights he accepts; at the outpost their value equals the platoon's presence after dark and the reaction behind it, and the enemy's answer to a better-armed post is to attack what is not rearmed (004 F004-1, F004-3, F004-16; §4.P1)
- **POS004-2** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, US.unit_quality, US.political_tolerance · In this war the ARVN and the RF/PF carry modern carbines from 1964, and the 1967 M16 crisis and inquiry and the 1968–69 rearmament do not occur; from 1969 the historical army has caught up, and the remaining difference is the squad gun, the marksman and the practice (004 F004-6; §4.P2–P4)
- **POS004-3** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, LOG.distribution · Abundant American ammunition from 1964 deepens the RVNAF's dependence on volume of fire; the 1974 ration falls hardest on the squad gun, and the divisional hoards built against it are lost in the collapse of March 1975 (004 F004-15; §4.P6)
- **POS005-1** · vars: STRIKE.responsiveness, FIND.main_force, FIX.capability · GPS weapons change what dies at a measured coordinate, never what can be located; in this war the J's precision is decisive where the enemy holds still long enough to be measured, at the siege and the fixed crossing, and adds nothing against the main force under canopy or the infrastructure in the hamlets (005 §2 F005-1, F005-7, F005-21)
- **POS005-2** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, FIX.capability, US.political_tolerance · In this war the defence of besieged positions from 1965 rests on the B-52J and an American coordinate cell; it is far stronger while American air power is present and leaves the RVNAF more dependent on it when it goes (005 §2 F005-20)
- **POS005-3** · vars: ENEMY.engagement_control, FIX.capability · In this war from Khe Sanh onward the PAVN does not lay a set-piece siege to a position the Americans can measure, until the conventional offensive of 1972 forces it to besiege An Loc and Kontum; it loses that one way of choosing its battles while the B-52J and the coordinate cell are present, and regains it when they leave in 1973 (005 §4.P3, §4.P5; EV000-41, EV000-76, EV000-77)
- **POSCP01-1** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.credibility_gap · The small gains on the American clock in memoranda 001–005 (no Tonkin deception, honest damage assessment, no M16 scandal, a conviction in 1967, fewer prisoners and no Bach Mai in 1972) narrow the credibility gap and do not move tolerance by a band in any phase, because the clock was spent by the casualties of 1965–68 and by Tet, which no provision changed and one made sharper (CP01 §3; C003-3)
- **POSCP01-2** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · In this war the American lever was used to protect the Republic's honest institutions from its own governments and never to make the Republic own the instruments of the conventional war (coordinates, reconnaissance, guided weapons, ammunition stocks); the dependence deepened by memoranda 004 and 005 was never contested by the instrument that could have contested it (CP01 §3)
- **POSCP01-3** · vars: ARVN.leadership, GVN.admin_capacity · The Commission, the Selection Board and every provision that needs a competent leader draw on one pool of perhaps 900–1,200 honest, able field-grade officers in 1964–66; the pool is spent several times over and the divisions are the loser each time, which is why G-4 stays open while the provinces improve (CP01 §3)
- **POS006-1** · vars: FIND.vci, VCI.strength, POP.night_control · Phung Hoang adds the layer above the hamlet to what the Special Branch knows, only where the night is held; outside the held belt it is the historical Phoenix whatever its rules, and its audited count, which falls where it works best, is the measure, never its arrest count (006 F006-15, F006-18, F006-26)
- **POS006-2** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.casualties, ENEMY.engagement_control · Unit rotation makes the American battalion fight better in the contacts it gets and changes neither which contacts it gets nor the late-war breakdown of discipline; it gives the enemy a relief window to aim at, and it does not prevent atrocity (006 F006-6, F006-16, F006-19)
- **POS006-3** · vars: ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · The selected advisory corps deepens influence, not authority; its durable values are continuity across the American unit's relief and honest reporting, and a better adviser deepens the advised unit's dependence on American fire unless he hands over the radio, which works for artillery, the VNAF and medevac and not for the B-52J (006 F006-2, F006-17, F006-23)
- **POS006-4** · vars: FIND.vci, INTEL.penetration, GVN.political_stability · In this war the national Phung Hoang file, built to warrant standard from 1964, was moved into the Central Intelligence Organization in 1970, consolidated in one building for the 1971 election, and captured intact on 30 April 1975 with the I Corps files a month earlier; the accuracy that made it valuable to the Republic made it more valuable to the victors (006 §4.P4, §4.P6; EV002-6, EV000-94, EV000-98)
- **POS006-5** · vars: FIND.vci, US.credibility_gap · In this war there was no ICEX, no Phoenix quota and no 1969 discovery of false claims; the attack on the infrastructure had an audited count from 1965, and "Phoenix" became a press scandal in March 1967 over the Duc Thanh raid rather than in 1970 over the programme (006 §4.P2, §4.P3; EV006-4, EV000-54)
- **POS007-1** · vars: ARVN.leadership, ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · In this war the ARVN's battalions from 1965–67 are commanded by officers a board chose on written criteria and two raters' reports, for eighteen months, with relief for cause; this puts ARVN effectiveness at the cap of the bands in 1966–68, and the enemy answers by declining the better battalion and attacking the unreformed unit beside it, so the gain appears as battalions not lost rather than in any metric (007 §4.P2; EV007-2, EV007-3)
- **POS007-2** · vars: ARVN.leadership, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · The ranked list for generals and division commands works only while the American aid condition protects it; in this war it filled one or two division commands in ten against the palace's preference by 1967, became advisory on 12 January 1970, and never governed the corps, so that the decisive commands of 1972 and 1975 were chosen as they were historically (007 §4.P4, §4.P5; EV007-4, EV007-5)
- **POS007-3** · vars: GVN.political_stability, ARVN.leadership, INTEL.penetration · An educated field-grade officer corps whose promotion is blocked at the top becomes a faction in the palace's eyes; in this war the colonels' petition of September 1970 was answered by moving about forty regimental and battalion commanders out of the field before Lam Son 719, and COSVN targeted the passed-over officers from 1968 with small yield (007 §4.P3, §4.P4; EV007-5, EV000-52)
- **POS007-4** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.casualties, POP.civilian_harm · American officer education from 1957 improves platoon and company leadership and saves American lives at a rate of perhaps one to three percent of small-unit deaths in 1965–69, below a band; it does not prevent My Lai or the late-war decay of discipline, which came from the command climate above the lieutenant (007 §4.P2, §4.P3; EV000-23)
- **REVMT01-1** · reverses POS001-3 · vars: HANOI.will, ENEMY.engagement_control, PAVN.strength_south · Hanoi's commitment to armed reunification is fixed throughout and nothing in the force reaches it (G-14); the timing of its offensives is not fixed, and the schedule of the last campaign in particular was set week by week by the ARVN's behaviour in 1975 (the plan for 1976 accelerated after Phuoc Long and again after the Highlands, EV000-92); a memorandum that changes the ARVN, the PAVN's losses or the Republic's state on the eve of the offensive must test what it does to that schedule (MT01 M-6, M-10, M-12)
- **POSMT01-1** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, VNAF.capability, ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.leadership · Rung (a) is reaffirmed after seven memoranda on its mechanism, not its date: every provision so far is American-owned and withdrawn by 1973, or works below the level of command at which 1972 and 1975 were decided, or was captured by the palace when the American lever lapsed in 1970–71; the rung will not move until a provision reaches an air arm the Republic owns, sustainment that survives the 1974 appropriation, or the choice of the corps commanders (MT01 M-12)
- **POSMT01-3** · vars: HANOI.will, PAVN.strength_south, ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · The date of the Republic's fall, 30 April 1975 within a window of about 27 April to the first days of May, is derived and not carried: it was set by Hanoi's resolution of 25 March to finish before the rains and by the 1st Corps' march, and only a delay of about three weeks or more in the collapse of I and II Corps would have moved it, by putting the assault into the rains; better ARVN units act on fights the PAVN bypasses and do not reach that threshold (MT01 M-12; EVMT01-4, EV000-96)
- **POSMT01-4** · vars: POP.night_control, VCI.strength, POP.gvn_legitimacy, FIND.vci · The countryside at the end of 1972 is not history's: where a PAVN division sat in the peopled lowlands (northern Binh Dinh, Quang Tri) the gains of 1964–71 were lost, while the held belt of the Delta and the Saigon region kept its posts and files and stays one band better at night and against the infrastructure; the government's legitimacy returns to history's through the decrees of 1972 (MT01 M-4; EVMT01-1, EVMT01-2, EVMT01-3)
- **POSMT01-5** · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.casualties, US.credibility_gap · The sum of the American lives the provisions saved is a judgment of about 2,500–5,000, mostly in 1965–69, five to nine percent of the historical dead, below a band; it does not move tolerance, and the changes in the record that bear on the 1974 appropriation roughly cancel, so the vote stands as history's until a provision changes what the Republic needs Congress to pay for (MT01 M-7; EV000-89)
- **POSMT01-6** · vars: ARVN.desertion, ARVN.effectiveness, POP.displacement · The ARVN's corps dissolved in March 1975 because the soldiers' families lived beside their units in the path of the offensive and the men went to them; no reform of the officer corps or the battalions reaches this, and it absorbed the gains of memoranda 004, 006 and 007 in the last campaign (MT01 open search; EV000-94, EV000-95)
- **POS008-1** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, ADVISE.leverage, US.political_tolerance · A domestic arsenal, battery works and rebuild depot stretch the aid dollar in 1974–75 only if the RVNAF has been made to buy from them while American supply was free; this headquarters adopts a domestic share enforced by the Aid Compliance Board from 1965, and the stretch changes what the fiscal 1975 appropriation buys, not the vote (008 §2 F008-2, F008-20, F008-23)
- **POS008-2** · vars: POP.night_control, RFPF.effectiveness, STRIKE.responsiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · A radio kept on the air at the post supplies the means of calling help in POSTNA-2 and moves the post's binding constraint to the reaction and fire within range; the Front answers by attacking the relief and the posts that cannot call, and the radio's gain appears as attacks not made (008 §2 F008-1, F008-3, F008-6, F008-16)
- **POS008-3** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, US.political_tolerance, HANOI.will · In this war the Republic's own arsenal and battery works stretched the fiscal 1975 appropriation to about $850 million–$1 billion of history's and kept its ammunition and communications from going dark in 1974, but delayed the collapse of I and II Corps by days, not the three weeks that would have moved the date; domestic sustainment without an air arm the Republic owns and a choice of corps commanders does not move the rung (008 §4.P6, §4.N; EV000-89, EVMT01-4)
- **POS008-4** · vars: RFPF.effectiveness, POP.night_control, STRIKE.responsiveness · From 1967 the territorial post's first call is for fire, not men, after the Front's ambush of the relief at My Phuoc Tay; this makes the post cheaper to hold and keeps the platoon behind its wire, so that the post is held better and the hamlet outside it is not, and the call passes to Vietnamese district guns in 1970–71 (008 §4.P2, §4.P4; EV008-4, EV008-7)
- **POS008-5** · vars: GVN.corruption, ADVISE.leverage, ARVN.self_sufficiency · The Directorate of Defence Industry fell to the palace in February 1970 with the four other institutions built behind the American lever; its output and the domestic share survived because the Joint General Staff wanted them, and honest lot acceptance did not, costing perhaps a tenth to a fifth of the base's 1974 value (008 §4.P4; EV002-6)
- **POS009-1** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, RFPF.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · Basic training changes how the fights the enemy accepts go and how many wounded live after them, never which fights he accepts; in this war the ARVN of 1964–65 stands a band above history on the course, the carbine and the educated lieutenant together, and the enemy answers the trained soldier with the mine, the sapper and the untrained target (009 §4.P1, §4.P2; EV002-2, EV009-2, EV009-4)
- **POS009-2** · vars: MED.survival, US.casualties, US.political_tolerance · In this war every soldier of both armies is taught the tourniquet in basic training; the saving is a judgment on a rate of two to four percent of killed in action, shown at Albany and in the first wave of Tet, about 900–1,900 Americans and 4,000–12,000 South Vietnamese, below a band on every variable and proof against enemy adaptation (009 §4.P2, §4.P3, §4.N; EV000-23, EV000-42)
- **POS009-3** · vars: ARVN.desertion, ECON.inflation, VCI.strength · Training does not reach desertion, which follows the soldier's pay, rice and family; the trained deserter carries the course home, and a few hundred a year in the Saigon belt carry it to the Front's guerrillas (009 §4.P2; EV009-3)
- **POS010-1** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, RFPF.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · In this war every RVNAF and territorial NCO since 1957 has passed the course for his grade, and empty squads are given to corporals first class who passed the leader's course; this changes how squads and posts fight the fights the enemy accepts, never which fights he accepts, and the enemy answers by passing the units that keep the routine and attacking those that do not, so the gain appears as companies not destroyed and posts not attacked (010 F010-19, F010-25; EV010-3, EV010-4)
- **POS010-2** · vars: ARVN.leadership, ADVISE.leverage, GVN.political_stability · The NCO promotion gate is a Vietnamese rule enforced by the training command and the boards below colonel; it was broken by the National Day decree of 1 November 1970 and repaired within a year by barring the next promotion, and it is the one merit rule of 1964 that survived the lapse of the American lever, because it threatened no one the palace cared about (010 EV010-6, F010-5)
- **POS010-4** · vars: ARVN.self_sufficiency, STRIKE.responsiveness · The American NCO course carries the habit of fixing the enemy and calling fire down to the ARVN squad; it is a strength the Republic owns only where the gun at the other end is Vietnamese, as at Long My, and a dependence everywhere else (010 F010-24; EV008-7)
- **POSCP02-1** · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · In this war the ARVN battalion of 1966–68 stands at the cap of the bands through four memoranda (007, 009, 010 and 004 before them), and the battalions broken in 1966–67 are about two-fifths to a half fewer than history's, a judgment whose factors overlap and whose upper bound is the "about half" of 010; any further provision on the battalion is measured in that running sum and not in the band, and none of it changes which fights the enemy accepts (CP02 §3, §5)
- **POSCP02-2** · vars: ENEMY.engagement_control, POP.civilian_harm, VCI.strength · Every provision since 004 that improved the RVNAF below the company was answered by the enemy moving his war to what the provision did not reach: the relief, the borrowed district, the mine in the hamlet, the untrained self-defence group; the provisions' gain in the army is paid for in part by the unprotected population, and every later provision touching the army or the posts names the target the enemy moves to and estimates the cost there (CP02 §1, §6; EV008-4, EV009-2, EV009-4, EV010-4)
- **REVR01-1** · reverses POSCP02-1 · vars: ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · The judgment of POSCP02-1 on the war stands: the ARVN battalions broken in 1966–67 are about two-fifths to a half fewer than history's, a judgment whose factors overlap and whose upper bound is the "about half" of 010, and none of it changes which fights the enemy accepts. What is reversed is its method: further provisions on the ARVN battalion are no longer measured outside the variable because the variable is capped. They are measured on the v1.0.6 scale, in the range of ARVN effectiveness and the facet they act on, and the running sum feeds that range (R01)
- **POS011-1** · vars: US.political_tolerance, NEGOT.position · In this war there is no Watergate: Nixon serves to January 1977, the Senate hearings, the Saturday Night Massacre, impeachment and resignation never happen, and the War Powers override fails; Case–Church still passes in June 1973 by veto-proof margins, so the end of American combat in Indochina on 15 August 1973 is law, and the binding constraint on American support from 1973 is Congress, not the President (011 F011-7, F011-9; EV000-86)
- **POS011-2** · vars: US.political_tolerance, ARVN.self_sufficiency · American military aid to the RVNAF is about $950 million for fiscal 1975, buying through the domestic stretch about what $1.2 billion bought historically, with supplementals of about $150 million in March and $175 million in May 1975 and about $800 million for fiscal 1976; the money reached fuel, aircraft and heavy rounds and saved perhaps 1,500–4,000 of the Republic's dead in 1974, and it never reached the soldier's pay or the artillery duel with the 130mm (011 F011-2, F011-21; EV000-89, EV000-91, EV011-2, EV000-97, EV011-3)
- **POS011-3** · vars: GVN.political_stability, ARVN.effectiveness, ARVN.desertion · Thieu refused the Dalat study on 11 March 1975 and gave no withdrawal order on 13–14 March, because he held the money and the President's message; the refusal cost half the Highland force and the 2nd Division and delayed the collapse of I and II Corps by three to five weeks, and in May he took the study's method for SOUTHERN WALL; the counter-directional finding is the mechanism of the gain (011 F011-20; EV000-94, EV000-95, EV011-3)
- **POS011-4** · vars: POP.civilian_harm, US.credibility_gap, US.unit_quality · The Son My massacre is removed by stipulation and isolated: there is no Peers inquiry, no Calley trial and no inquiry into the Americal Division's command climate, every other killing of civilians in Quang Ngai stands, and Son My's people live under the Front; the public's verdict on the war is unchanged because it was in before November 1969 (011 F011-5, F011-10, F011-11; EV000-46, EV000-63, EV000-72)
- **POS011-5** · vars: US.unit_quality, US.political_tolerance, US.casualties · A quarter of the historically inducted enlisted voluntarily in the same jobs (Reading A); draft calls are a quarter smaller and the force is unchanged; the volunteers die at the draftees' rate and are about half as likely to be on the drug and refusal lists of 1970–71, with no change to any battle (011 F011-15, F011-19; EV010-5)
- **REV011-1** · reverses POSMT01-3 · vars: HANOI.will, PAVN.strength_south, ARVN.effectiveness, ENEMY.engagement_control · The method of POSMT01-3 stands: the date of the fall is derived from Hanoi's calendar, and only a delay of about three weeks or more in the collapse of I and II Corps moves it. What is reversed is the date. In this war the collapse came three to five weeks late, because Thieu gave no withdrawal order on 13–14 March 1975; the Politburo put the assault on Saigon back to the dry season of 1975–76, and the fall is expected between February and May 1976 (011; EVMT01-4, EV000-94, EV000-95)
- **REV011-2** · reverses POSMT01-5 · vars: US.political_tolerance, US.casualties, US.credibility_gap · The sum of the American lives saved stands at about 3,700–7,800 and does not move tolerance. What is reversed is the vote: the fiscal 1975 appropriation is no longer history's, because the President who fought for it was not fighting impeachment, and the April 1975 request is Nixon's and partly voted (011 F011-17; EV000-89, EV000-97)

- **P006a** · Phung Hoang (Phoenix) Programme, formalized 1 January 1964 and built to 2026 practice: a national Phung Hoang Committee, Province and District Intelligence and Operations Coordinating Centres (PIOCC and DIOCC) in every province and district, an F3EAD targeting cycle with network analysis and document exploitation, SEEK II-class biometric enrolment of detainees and ralliers, warrant-based targeting under the 1964 police statute, the Provincial Reconnaissance Units raised under that statute, capture-first rules, no quotas, and an independent audit of neutralization claims · One national programme [U]: a national committee and centre, 44 PIOCCs and about 240 DIOCCs at full coverage [E: the period's province and district count], of which about 20 PIOCCs and 100 DIOCCs by end 1964 and all by end 1965 [E: the security-limited occupation of P002a's posts]; about 4,000–5,000 Vietnamese staff in the centres [E: 10–15 per DIOCC, 25–40 per PIOCC, about 150 nationally]; about 1,500 biometric kits [E: one per district station and centre plus field teams] · spaces ~600 US personnel, of whom ~450 military spaces [E: one or two advisers per DIOCC in contested districts, three per PIOCC, a national cell of about 60, an exploitation and analysis detachment of about 80, about 40 biometrics contractors] · FIND, FIX, SUBVERT, SECURE, ADVISE · arrives 1964-01-01 · active · memo 006

## Gap register (latest status)

- **G-1** · A state without a foundation · narrowed · Land, police, merit chiefs and the Commission give the Republic a government in the held belt from 1964; it is captured by the palace when the American lever lapses in 1970–71, and its foundation in the countryside does not carry into the conventional war (CP01)
- **G-2** · Who holds the countryside after dark · narrowed · Posts with a radio, a schooled leader, a trained platoon and a call for fire hold the held belt at night and are passed by an enemy who reads their routine; the hamlet outside the wire, the borrowed district and the contested belt are unchanged, and the enemy's war moves to them (CP02)
- **G-3** · Identifying the infrastructure inside the population · narrowed · A Special Branch, a census and a land register identify the infrastructure in the held belt from 1964 and drive it out; it moves to the towns, penetrates the Branch, and turns the census into the Hue lists (CP01)
- **G-4** · The officer corps: selection, leadership, desertion, corruption · narrowed · Below the regiment the RVNAF is led by board-chosen, educated officers and schooled NCOs from 1965–66, two-fifths to a half fewer battalions are broken in 1966–67, and the enemy declines them; the divisions and corps stay the palace's choices, and the decisive commands of 1972 and 1975 are chosen as historically (CP02)
- **G-5** · The American political clock · open · The provisions saved perhaps 2,500–5,000 American lives, below a band; tolerance unmoved in every phase, and the 1974 appropriation now examined and unmoved (MT01)
- **G-6** · Advisory leverage and its limits · open · The Aid Compliance Board is a real lever until 1969 and lapses with the withdrawal; it was used for governance and never for the RVNAF's self-sufficiency (CP01)
- **G-7** · Finding and fixing the main force · open · The enemy is easier to see in the open and exactly as hard to find under canopy; he still chooses every fight except the siege (CP01)
- **G-8** · Sanctuary and the theory of attrition · open · Cambodia is counted from 1965 and its caches fall in ten days in 1970; the sanctuaries still regenerate the main force in every phase (CP01)
- **G-9** · The Trail: throughput required against capacity · open · Measured from 1965 instead of guessed; bombing taxes it by about a tenth at best, and the B-52J built it a net with no single point of failure (CP01)
- **G-10** · The measurement problem · narrowed · The radar's ledger, the musters and the Phoenix audit give honest counts of the Trail, the army and the infrastructure, and the audit is the palace's after 1970; the provisions' largest gain, attacks not made on better units and posts, appears in no count of either army, and ARVN effectiveness at the cap hides every further increment (CP02)
- **G-11** · The sea and Sihanoukville · narrowed · The sea route closed in 1964; Sihanoukville opened eighteen months early and was counted, not stopped, until Lon Nol closed it in 1970 (CP01)
- **G-12** · Air power against a dispersed, night-moving enemy · narrowed · Decisive against the measured siege and the fixed crossing; nothing against a regiment under canopy or an attack on a post at night, and none of it Vietnamese (CP01)
- **G-13** · No single manager of the war · open · CORDS on its historical date and form; the provisions created no single manager, only better inheritances for it (CP01)
- **G-14** · No lever on Hanoi's will · open · Nothing in the force reaches the Politburo; the timing of its last campaign was its own, set by the 1st Corps' road and the rains, and only a three-week delay in the collapse of I and II Corps would have moved it (MT01)
- **G-15** · The theater base · open · Unchanged by any provision; the rearmament's ammunition and the J's kits ride the historical base (CP01)
- **G-16** · Personnel spaces · narrowed · Unit rotation, a selected eighteen-month advisory corps, drill sergeants and NCO schools draw on one pool of American senior NCOs, bringing the 1967 shortage forward three to six months and deepening it; spaces remain trivial against a ceiling of none, and nothing a provision has built survives the withdrawal of 1973 (CP02)
- **G-17** · The soldier's family · open · The devaluation of June 1966 cut the private's rice by a third and his trained desertion carried the course to the Front around Saigon; no provision has touched pay against inflation, dependants' housing or the movement of families, and in March 1975 the corps dissolved toward them (CP02)

## Study: Air War (`studies/air-war.md`)
*Written ST01 · reflects the record after memo 011 · last folded — · tags: AIR.north_effect, AIR.north_defences, AIR.losses, VNAF.capability, STRIKE.responsiveness, TRAIL.capacity, TRAIL.tonnage_arriving, SANCT.laos, SANCT.cambodia, ARVN.effectiveness.fire_coordination, ARVN.self_sufficiency.fire_support, POP.civilian_harm*

### Summary
The air war in this record is history's air war with two new instruments in it, and its shape is set by one fact: American air power became far better at destroying what it could measure, and the enemy, within a season each time, stopped owning anything that could be measured. The two instruments arrived on the war's first day. The first was eyes: two U-2S Dragon Ladies and four RQ-4B Global Hawks (P003a, P003b), working under the standing condition that gives them GPS and satellite links (E01), so that from January 1964 the enemy's roads, passes, fuel dumps, missile sites and assembly areas were watched in any weather and counted every night. The second was a hand: every B-52 replaced one for one by the re-engined B-52J with the AN/APQ-188 radar (P005a), carrying the GBU-31 and GBU-38 Joint Direct Attack Munitions (P005b, P005c) and the Quickstrike family of influence mines (P005d), and fed from March 1964 by a coordinate cell at Tan Son Nhut under Major Edwin T. Sorrell that turned imagery into aimpoints true to a few metres (EV005-1).

Between them they changed four things, and each change was real. First, the war's interdiction debate became honest five years early: the panhandle watch counted the Trail's trucks from December 1965 (EV003-3), the Sihanoukville count settled in March 1967 an argument history settled only with captured ledgers in 1970 (EV003-4), and from 1969 every Commando Hunt claim travelled to Washington beside a radar count that never let the claim that more trucks had died than existed survive a season (EV000-55, EV000-68). Second, a siege the enemy dug became the enemy's worst battle: Con Thien lifted about three weeks early in 1967, Khe Sanh about two weeks early in 1968 with perhaps 3,500–4,000 PAVN dead to July against about 2,469 acknowledged, and in 1972 the J's cells broke the penetration of An Loc on 12 May and the assault on Kontum short of the wire (EVCP02-3, EV000-41, EV000-76, EV000-77) [X-005]. Third, the air war over the North, when Washington finally allowed it in 1972, chose from folders seven years in the making: the Thanh Hoa bridge fell on the first night of Freedom Train, and Linebacker II cost about six bombers rather than fifteen and did not hit Bach Mai or Kham Thien Street (EV000-75, EV000-82) [X-005]. Fourth, a handful of single events went the other way from history because a radar watched them: Pierce Arrow was never flown after the false alarm of 4 August 1964, and Neak Luong was never bombed in August 1973 (EV000-3, EV000-86).

None of that reached the three things that decided the war, and the record says so as plainly as it records the gains. The enemy's flow south was taxed, never stopped. HARD CROSSING cut every bridge in the panhandle in 1966 and taxed the flow by 10–15 percent for a few weeks; by the autumn Group 559 had built a braided net of fords, causeways and pontoons with no single point of failure, and from then on the panhandle was harder to cut than history's ever was (EV005-2, POS005-4). The study judges tonnage arriving in the South a trace below history's at most in every phase from 1966 to 1972, and the Trail's capacity one to three points above history's from 1966 to the end, which is the measured price of the J's precision against a labour-rich enemy (G-9). The main force under canopy was found no better than history found it, and the air war's precision added nothing against it (POS003-1, POS005-1). And none of the instruments belonged to the Republic. The U-2S, the Global Hawks, the cell, the folders and the bombers all went home in 1973; the Joint General Staff asked to keep a coordinate cell and there was nothing in the VNAF for it to send coordinates to (EV000-86). The ARVN had learned, at Lolo and Sophia, An Loc and Kontum, to hold a besieged position and wait for the bombs, and in 1974 it waited at Thuong Duc for a siege box that no longer existed (EV000-91). At Phuoc Long the province chief's plan asked for "the B-52 support provided for in the plan" by the call signs of 1972 (EV000-92).

So the margin over history is large inside the air war and small outside it. Over the North and on the Trail it is a better-informed, more precise and less costly version of the same campaign against the same rules, with the same result. In the South it is a set of besieged positions held more cheaply while the Americans were there and an army more dependent on them when they left, which the study judges as the Republic's own fire support standing up to three points below history's at the end of 1972 (P5). The one place the air war's balance turns in the Republic's favour is late and indirect: in 1974–75 a larger appropriation kept a third more of the VNAF flying, and its transports and helicopters carried the relief of Phu Loc, the counter-attack at Phuoc An and three weeks of the siege of Pleiku (EV000-91, EV000-95). At the end of 1975 the Republic still has an air force, which history's did not, and it still cannot break a siege with it. The gap register's sentence on air power stands at its true weight in both directions: decisive against the measured siege and the fixed crossing, nothing against a regiment under canopy or an attack on a post at night, and none of it Vietnamese (G-12).

### Questions for the record
- **Q-1** · CHECKPOINT · EV000-53 (history/chapters/P3.md, origin HIST) carries Rolling Thunder's historical sorties and its 922 aircraft lost unaltered, while P003a and P005a push AIR.losses −1 (memos 003 and 005 manifests) and EVCP02-2 alters the losses of Spring High; no chapter states Rolling Thunder's losses in this war, and the checkpoint should either alter EV000-53 or state that the pushes did not reach the northern campaign before 1972.
- **Q-2** · CHECKPOINT · EV000-68 (history/chapters/P4.md) sets the radar's Commando Hunt V net loss of about 8–10% against "the phases' own historical estimate falling to about 2 percent" and attributes only one or two points to the J; the chapter does not say whether the remaining difference is a better effect (radar-cued gunships) or a better measurement of the same effect, which decides whether TRAIL.tonnage_arriving in P4 should sit nearer −2 than this study's −1..0.
- **Q-3** · CHECKPOINT · EV003-3 (history/chapters/P2.md, written by memorandum 003) still says that on 12 April 1966 "B-52s struck the Mu Gia pass for the first time [H]; the orbit watched the first trucks move through the craters about twenty hours later", which is history's unguided strike; EV005-2 (memorandum 005) has the Js cut every crossing that night and keep them down for six weeks. The STEADY COUNT sentence was never brought into line and should be reconciled at the next consolidation.
- **Q-4** · CHECKPOINT · The record holds no account of the air war in northern Laos after December 1964 (Barrel Roll, the Plain of Jars, the Lima Sites), of the air war in the South by tactical aircraft (close air support sorties and their fall with the withdrawal), or of the VNAF between Rolling Thunder's first day and 1974; no variable captures the weight of American air power in the South, and STRIKE.responsiveness measures speed, not weight. Whether to add such a variable is a version change.
- **Q-5** · CHECKPOINT · ARVN.effectiveness.fire_coordination is unjudged in every chapter though the record holds evidence on it (EV000-71, EV000-76, EV000-77, EV000-91, F007-23); judging it needs the binding facet of ARVN.effectiveness in each phase, which the next checkpoint should name.
- **Q-6** · CHECKPOINT · POP.civilian_harm has no holder: it is pushed by twelve provisions and judged nowhere, and its decisive differences (P011c; the Highlands column of EV000-95) lie outside any study so far; a checkpoint or a study of the population should judge it.
